_comment: Permission profile for sh/claude_confined.sh only. Loaded via `claude --settings`,
so it applies to sandboxed sessions and to nothing else. A normal `claude` launch
never reads this file and keeps the usual prompting.
Everything here is allowed because the bubblewrap sandbox is the real boundary:
the repository is the only writable path, so a permitted command cannot reach
outside it. Deletions still ask, because the sandbox cannot tell a wanted delete
from an unwanted one inside the repository.
Deny rules always win, and they cannot be overridden from here. The user-level
settings deny curl, wget, ssh, scp, rsync, git push and sudo, so those stay
blocked in a confined session too. Lift them in that file if you want them.
Cloning asks, and it has to ask here rather than rely on the domain allowlist.
sh/fetch.sh enforces that list by parsing the host, but it only governs itself:
WebFetch(domain:...) rules bind the WebFetch tool, never a Bash command. A git
clone is a Bash command, the allow list above is a bare `Bash`, and the sandbox
cannot filter network egress on this cluster -- so without the rule below a
clone of any repository at all would run unprompted. The same applies to
`gh repo clone` and `git submodule add`, which reach the network the same way.
git clean asks because `git clean -xdf` here would delete workbench/ and its
.git. The private repository is gitignored, -x removes ignored files, and it is
the one tree in this project that would not regenerate. See notes/docs/SPLIT.md.
Pattern matching only catches the common spellings. A delete routed through an
interpreter (python -c 'os.remove(...)') or a clobbering git checkout will not
prompt. Nor will `git -C dir clone`, which does not start with the matched
prefix. These rules raise the cost of a mistake; they are not a boundary.
enabledPlugins is repeated here, and it has to be. Deny rules union across every
settings layer, so they survive `--settings` -- verified 2026-09-10 by running
`curl --version` in a confined session and being refused. enabledPlugins does NOT
union: this file wins outright, and while it lacked the key NO plugin loaded, so
every plugin skill silently disappeared the moment confinement was switched on.
Nothing was uninstalled and nothing said anything -- the skills were simply not
there. The seven below are the merge of three files: caveman from
$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json, ck from .claude/settings.json, and the five
official ones from .claude/settings.local.json. Change a plugin anywhere and it
must be changed here too, or a confined session will not have it.
extraKnownMarketplaces is repeated for the same reason: without it the three
marketplaces the plugins come from cannot be resolved.
